precepts.text: He that openeth, and no man shutteth; and shutteth, and no man openeth: that was Christ. So right now repentance is open. Longsuffering. That's the time right now to get it right. Once that door is closed, that's it. No one can open it. That great gulf fixed.
precepts.point: We read this all the time, but you don't understand what Noah dealt with. There's babies out there. People: please, my baby, please. Screaming and crying. His family out there too; Noah had siblings, sons and daughters out there screaming: why are you doing this? Noah had to sit there and take it, hear the screaming, the crying, the begging, until you hear nothing no more. That's a terrible thing to experience, man.

note.label: As in the Days of Noah: Past & Present

precepts.why:
Genesis 7 ends with four words: “and the Lord shut him in.” Noah did not close that door; God did. Revelation 3:7 shows who holds that power: “he that openeth, and no man shutteth; and shutteth, and no man openeth.” That is Christ, the one “that hath the key of David.”

Why did God close the door himself? Because of what Noah would hear outside. Noah was a man, and a man has a soft spot. There were babies out there, people begging for their babies, screaming and crying. Noah's own kin were out there too, his siblings and relatives, crying out, why are you doing this? If the door were left to Noah, he might have opened it. So God said, get back, I'll close the door. Noah had to sit inside and hear the screaming, the crying and the begging until there was nothing to hear anymore. That is a terrible thing to live through.

The door was shut only after a long season of mercy. Noah was a hundred years building that boat, and the people were warned the whole time: repent, stop following Cain, keep these laws. They said, we good. God was longsuffering with them. Noah was found righteous “in this generation” because he kept the commandments; that is how he knew the clean beasts from the unclean and how he walked with God. When the fountains of the great deep broke up and the windows of heaven opened, only the eight souls on that boat lived.

It is the same today. Right now the door of repentance is open, and Christ is longsuffering with our people. This is the time to get it right. Once that door is closed, that is it; no one can open it, the way the great gulf is fixed. As it was in the days of Noah, so it is now.

precepts.text: God spared not the old world, but saved Noah the eighth person, a preacher of righteousness, bringing in the flood upon the world of the ungodly. Noah was righteous because he preached and kept the commandments. He was the eighth person because a true captain put his wife, his sons, and their wives on first and got on last. Men of God have to be strong; we come to the Sabbath because we are sick, surrounded by the world all week.
precepts.point: All flesh died that moved upon the earth, fowl, cattle, beast, every creeping thing, and every man in whose nostrils was the breath of life, and every living substance was destroyed. Why would God kill innocent animals? I do not know and I do not care; he has a reason for all destruction. We do not have to worry about why these wars are going. God set it up, so keep the commandments and he will deliver us. A lot more than eight will make it this time, but very few, so do not be surprised when your family will not listen at camp.

note.label: Wars Are Here: Seek Good Not Evil

precepts.why:
God told Noah, “Come thou and all thy house into the ark; for thee have I seen righteous before me in this generation.” Why was Noah chosen to be delivered with his family? Peter explains it: God “spared not the old world, but saved Noah the eighth person, a preacher of righteousness, bringing in the flood upon the world of the ungodly”.

The old world is the world we read about in Genesis 7, and God did not spare it: he killed all flesh. Noah was righteous because he preached righteousness and kept the commandments. He was a godly man in an ungodly world, and he had received his orders from God on exactly how to build the ark and did it faithfully. His standing up for God is what brought the flood in upon the ungodly.

Why is he called the eighth person? The other seven were his wife, his three sons, Shem, Ham and Japheth, and their wives. Noah is counted eighth because a true captain, a true leader, made sure his wife, his sons and their wives were on first, and he was the last one to get on the ark. When Noah gave the word, they did not question him; they got on.

That is why men of God have to be strong. We come to the Sabbath because we are sick. We are surrounded by the world all week and fighting the sin around us and in our own thoughts, so we need to be around brothers and sisters who will correct us in righteousness.

The flood shows the mind of God for destruction. Nobody was righteous except the ones on the ark. The coming destruction, a thermonuclear war, will be on another level, and we want to be spiritually the men and women in that ark, not the ones drowning. A lot more than eight will make it this time, but very few, so do not be surprised when your family does not listen. Keep the commandments, preach righteousness, and God will deliver us.

precepts.text: The law of the beasts makes a difference between the unclean and the clean, the beast that may be eaten and the beast that may not be eaten.
precepts.point: The beasts went in male and female to keep seed alive upon the face of all the earth, so that they could repopulate once the earth dried up; nature itself tells you what we should and should not be doing.

note.label: Genesis 7: The First Rain and the Flood

precepts.why:
Noah was told to take “Of every clean beast” by sevens and “of beasts that are not clean by two”. The dietary law was not yet instituted, but the Most High had already defined what was a clean beast and what was an unclean beast, all the way back in Genesis. Noah knew the difference.

Moses reiterated that law to the children of Israel: “This is the law of the beasts, and of the fowl, and of every living creature that moveth in the waters, and of every creature that creepeth upon the earth: To make a difference between the unclean and the clean, and between the beast that may be eaten and the beast that may not be eaten.” It is tied to holiness: “ye shall therefore be holy, for I am holy.”

Today this gets confused with the doctrine that says I can eat all things through Christ who strengthens me, and that is not true. The laws were instituted for us to discern between the unclean and the clean, and that difference was already known in Noah’s day.

precepts.text: The people are taught to discern between the unclean and the clean; that is what the laws were instituted for.
precepts.point: The beasts went in male and female to keep seed alive upon the face of all the earth, so that they could repopulate once the earth dried up; nature itself tells you what we should and should not be doing.

note.label: Genesis 7: The First Rain and the Flood

precepts.why:
“And they shall teach my people the difference between the holy and profane, and cause them to discern between the unclean and the clean.” That is what the laws were instituted for: so the people would discern between the unclean and the clean, the same distinction Noah was given at the ark, clean beasts by sevens and unclean by two.

It is not true that we can eat all things through Christ who strengthens us. The people are still to be taught the difference. The beasts went in male and female “to keep seed alive upon the face of all the earth”, so they could repopulate once the earth dried up; nature itself tells you what we should and should not be doing.

precepts.text: The Most High had not caused it to rain upon the earth; a mist watered the whole face of the ground.
precepts.point: Up until this point it had never rained on the earth; a mist went up from the earth and watered the ground. Understand the faith Noah had to have, being told to build an ark because it was going to rain, a thing that had never happened.

note.label: Genesis 7: The First Rain and the Flood

precepts.why:
When the Most High said “I will cause it to rain upon the earth forty days and forty nights”, it had never rained on the earth. Go back to the beginning: “the Lord God had not caused it to rain upon the earth”. Instead “there went up a mist from the earth, and watered the whole face of the ground.” That mist is how the ground was watered up until this point.

Understand the faith Noah had to have. He was told to build an ark because it was going to rain, a thing that had never happened. He built it anyway.

precepts.text: The flood came upon them that despised the commandments, and Noah alone was left with his household, of whom came all righteous men.
precepts.point: The breath of life is twofold. One is the commandments, which were given to Adam; the other is the breathing life, the oxygen. Here everything on the dry land that breathed died; the fish were not touched.

note.label: Genesis 7: The First Rain and the Flood

precepts.why:
Ezra tells why the flood came. “And every people walked after their own will, and did wonderful things before thee, and despised thy commandments. And again in process of time thou broughtest the flood upon those that dwelt in the world, and destroyedst them.” This was the first time the Most High destroyed the earth for the wickedness that was being done. The flood came because they despised the commandments; destruction came because of sin.

“And it came to pass in every of them, that as death was to Adam, so was the flood to these.” Of them that dwelt in the world “Nevertheless one of them thou leftest, namely, Noah with his household, of whom came all righteous men.” That is Genesis 7:23, Noah only remaining alive with them that were with him in the ark.

From Noah’s household came all righteous men: through Shem’s seed to Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, and through their line the Israelites.

precepts.text: The Most High breathed into Adam the breath of life; that breath is the commandments.
precepts.point: The breath of life is twofold. One is the commandments, which were given to Adam; the other is the breathing life, the oxygen. Here everything on the dry land that breathed died; the fish were not touched.

note.label: Genesis 7: The First Rain and the Flood

precepts.why:
Genesis says all “in whose nostrils was the breath of life, of all that was in the dry land, died.” The breath of life is twofold. Ezra says the Most High gave “a body unto Adam without soul, which was the workmanship of thine hands, and didst breathe into him the breath of life, and he was made living before thee.” One breath of life is the commandments, which were given to Adam; the other is the breathing life, the oxygen.

Here in the flood, everything on the dry land that breathed died. The fish were not touched.

precepts.text: Keep my commandments, and live; the commandments are the breath of life.
precepts.point: The breath of life is twofold. One is the commandments, which were given to Adam; the other is the breathing life, the oxygen. Here everything on the dry land that breathed died; the fish were not touched.

note.label: Genesis 7: The First Rain and the Flood

precepts.why:
“Keep my commandments, and live; and my law as the apple of thine eye.” The commandments are the breath of life. That is the first side of the breath of life the Most High breathed into Adam: keep the commandments and live.

The people of Noah’s day despised the commandments, and so all in whose nostrils was the breath of life on the dry land died. Destruction came because of sin.
